chunks: And from him, from his two brothers, from their father, from Thalabah, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya ibn Bassam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

We asked him about a man who says: 'If I buy so-and-so, he is free; and if I buy this garment, it is for the poor; and if I marry so-and-so, she is divorced.' He said: 'That is nothing. A man does not divorce except what he owns, nor free except what he owns, nor give charity except with what he owns.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a conditional divorce or manumission statement to be legally valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of conditional declarations (al-shurut) is clarified by emphasizing that legal efficacy depends on actual ownership (milkiyyah) at the time of utterance. This establishes a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence that one cannot dispose of what one does not possess, preventing invalidity in divorce, manumission, and charity. The hadith underscores the precision required in verbal contracts, ensuring that conditional statements are not merely hypothetical but grounded in tangible possession.
